No git. Use the diff file.

## DEFECT: Same-model retries after a wire cut lose exponential backoff when no hold is spent

**Mechanism.** `turn-recovery.ts:2806-2810` picks the backoff from `connectionHoldCandidate`, which is the output of `#holdsChainForConnectionRetry`. It does not use whether a hold is actually spent:

- `connectionHoldCandidate ? calculateFullJitterRetryDelayMs(base, heldRetryIndex) : calculateRetryBackoffDelayMs(base, this.#retryAttempt)`
- `heldRetryIndex = #connectionHoldsSpent + 1`.

A hold is only spent at line 3125-3126, inside `chainConsultable && connectionHold`. When that branch doesn't run, `heldRetryIndex` never moves past 1. The cases are:
- `retry.modelFallback` is off, or no chain is configured. This is the default setup.
- No selector.
- The chain doesn't admit the failure.

In those cases every candidate retry still takes full jitter over `[0, base)`. The candidate rule covers attempts 1 and 2. Attempt 2 should get `[0.75, 1] × 2·base`, but here it can be close to 0 ms. The comment at 3121-3124 says such a retry "stays on the model anyway and holds nothing", so the backoff change is not intended. The same thing happens when a chain is configured but the consult doesn't switch: the retry keeps the full-jitter delay instead of the normal backoff.

**Who is affected.** Every `anthropic`, `openai-codex-responses` or `cursor` session without a fallback chain that hits a statusless wire cut on a request sent once. On main, attempt 1 waited ≈375–500 ms and attempt 2 ≈750–1000 ms at the default base. At this head both waits fall in `[0, 500)`. That is the clustered immediate replay the full-jitter comment says it is avoiding.

**Trigger.** I used the harness from `agent-session-wire-retry-requests.test.ts`, with:
- `retry.modelFallback: false`
- `retry.baseDelayMs: 1000`, `retry.maxDelayMs: 30000`
- Script: two `cutAfterReasoning` responses, then `ok`.

Probe: `scratch/probe/nochain.test.ts`, run with `-t PROBE`.

**Measured.** The `auto_retry_start` delays were `[711.66, 940.49]` and, on a rerun, `[587.86, 886.02]`. Both second delays are below 1000 ms. The backoff on main can't go under 1500 ms for attempt 2 at base 1000. Three requests were sent, all to the primary model, and no hold was spent.

**Fix.** Pick full jitter only when the hold is actually taken, i.e. `chainConsultable && connectionHold`. Every other path should keep `calculateRetryBackoffDelayMs(base, #retryAttempt)`.

## NOT A DEFECT

**Earlier findings, checked at this head** (`scratch/probe/closure.test.ts`, run from `packages/ai`, exit 0):
- **Astra P1 (a trailing `retry-after-ms` creating a permanent block): closed.**
  - `extractProviderRetryHint` and `providerRetryWaitMs` read the first wait in the text. Both `…200 tail retry-after-ms=86400000` and the 72-nines variant now read 200.
  - The header's wait reaches consumers only as a structured value (`errorRetryAfterMs`, or headers on a thrown error).
  - `markReached` caps a stated wait at `MAX_HINTED_BLOCK_MS`, which is 7 days.
- **Astra P2 (decoration suffixes): closed for the reported inputs.** `read ECONNRESET after 401 nsec`, `[fe80::1%eth0]:401` and `after 403分` are now Connection and retriable.
- **Astra P3 (`terminated` followed by a reason): closed.** All four reason forms now have Connection false, so they can't earn a hold.
  - Their `retriable: true` comes from `terminated` in the existing `TRANSIENT_TRANSPORT_PATTERN`. This change didn't add that.
  - Bare `terminated` and `terminated (https://h/v1)` are still Connection.
- **Claude P3 (no limit on how long a block lasts): closed** by `MAX_HINTED_BLOCK_MS` in `RateLimits.markReached`.
- **Claude P3 (quoted upstream `retry-after-ms=9000`): closed.** The text now reads 200. Only `longestProviderRetryHint` reads 9000, and it can only turn down a hold.
- **Claude P3 (header `x-ratelimit-reset` reaching long-lived blocks): bounded, not removed.** Durable consumers still take the larger of the header and the text, as the change intends, but the block is now capped at 7 days.
- **Claude P4 (hold wait ≥ durable wait): no longer applies.** Durable readers now use the first value in the text, so the hold check (longest value) always declines at or above it.

**Suspicions I ruled out:**
- `abortRetry()` cancellation mark outliving its saga. The success path (`turn-recovery.ts:976-978`), `#endCancelledRetry` and new prompts all go through `resolveRetry()`, which clears the mark. The mark is also tied to the prompt generation.
- `withWireCount` in `withReplaySafeStreamRetry` giving direct-call providers a counted global `fetch`. When `fetch` was undefined, those providers already fell back to the runtime `fetch`, so behaviour is the same.
- gitlab-duo's `getDirectAccessToken(options.fetch)` counting toward the request. It can only report one replay too many, which turns down a hold (the safe direction). It never causes an extra hold.

**Environment notes:**
- My first probe run failed module resolution from the scratch directory. A `node_modules` symlink in scratch fixed it.
- The probe's 3-iteration loop hit a stack overflow because `mockSchedulerWaitWithClock` was set up again on every pass. The first iteration's measurement is valid, and I took a second sample with a separate run.
